notes: All historical amounts are in absolute USD (converted from SEC “in millions”); EBIT is modeled as Operating profit from TI’s Consolidated Statements of Income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))

D&A is defined as (Depreciation + Amortization of capitalized software) because TI discloses them separately within cash flow adjustments. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))

NWC is constructed at each fiscal year-end as: (Total current assets - cash and cash equivalents - short-term investments) - (Total current liabilities - current portion of long-term debt). This excludes cash-like investments and current debt to keep NWC closer to operating working capital. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))

Base-case forecast drivers are modeled assumptions (recovery then gradual stabilization) rather than explicit year-by-year company guidance; capex intensity is anchored to TI’s stated expectation to spend about $2B to $3B in 2026 (used qualitatively to justify the capex decline). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))

NOL: TI discloses tax loss carryforwards were not material as of Dec 31, 2025; therefore nol_balance is set to null and utilization percent is left at a placeholder value. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))
Current price uses the latest quote timestamped March 21, 2026 from the finance tool.

catalysts: Synergy and execution progress from the announced acquisition of Silicon Labs (cash offer $231.00/share; expected close in first half of 2027; ~$450M annual synergies within three years post-close). ([ti.com](https://www.ti.com/about-ti/newsroom/news-releases/2026/2026-02-04-texas-instruments-to-acquire-silicon-labs.html))

Quarterly upside/downside relative to Q1 2026 revenue/EPS guidance as demand trends through analog and embedded demand cycles. ([ti.com](https://www.ti.com/about-ti/newsroom/news-releases/2026/2026-01-27-ti-reports-q4-2025-and-2025-financial-results-and-shareholder-returns.html))
Further disclosure on 2026 capex pace and manufacturing ramp impacts to utilization and margin.
company_overview: Texas Instruments designs and manufactures analog and embedded processing semiconductors used across industrial, automotive, communications, and data-center end markets.
Business is reported across Analog, Embedded Processing, and Other segments, with profit driven by demand/utilization, cost structure, and mix.
The company emphasizes scale manufacturing capability (including 300mm fabs) and ongoing capital investment cycles supported by recurring cash generation.
current_context: Q4 2025 revenue was $4.423B with operating profit of $1.473B; FY2025 revenue was $17.682B with diluted EPS of $5.45. ([ti.com](https://www.ti.com/about-ti/newsroom/news-releases/2026/2026-01-27-ti-reports-q4-2025-and-2025-financial-results-and-shareholder-returns.html))

Management guided Q1 2026 revenue of $4.32B to $4.68B and EPS of $1.22 to $1.48. ([ti.com](https://www.ti.com/about-ti/newsroom/news-releases/2026/2026-01-27-ti-reports-q4-2025-and-2025-financial-results-and-shareholder-returns.html))
Company-wide cash flow from operations in FY2025 was $7.153B and capital expenditures were $4.55B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))
investment_highlights: Base-case thesis ties operating profitability to a cyclical recovery: EBIT margin is modeled to settle back toward the upper end of the historical range as utilization normalizes.

Capex intensity declines after the elevated spend period, consistent with management stating capex expected to be about $2B to $3B in 2026. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))
Working capital intensity is held as a % of sales and then gradually mean-reverts to reflect steadier operating cycles.
Peer-comparable valuation is used to anchor terminal value via an exit EV/EBITDA multiple.
key_risks: Semiconductor cyclicality: demand slowdowns could reduce revenue growth and pressure utilization, lowering EBIT margin below base-case.
Cost/mix and competitive pricing risk could compress gross margin and operating profit despite revenue stabilization.

M&A execution and integration risks (regulatory approvals, deal timing, and synergy realization) following the Silicon Labs transaction. ([ti.com](https://www.ti.com/about-ti/newsroom/news-releases/2026/2026-02-04-texas-instruments-to-acquire-silicon-labs.html))

presentation.subtitle: TXN DCF Inputs (FY25 base-case) + Peer Multiples
valuation_summary: DCF uses FY2023–FY2025 GAAP operating structure (revenue, operating profit as EBIT, depreciation & amortization, capex, and a consistent NWC construction). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000059/txn-20251231.htm))
Terminal value uses an exit-multiple framework (EV/EBITDA) and a modest long-run growth rate to remain economically sensible for a developed-market analog/embedded business.

Peer multiples (EV/EBITDA and forward P/E) are included to sanity-check whether the terminal assumptions imply a reasonable valuation relative to large semis. ([alphaspread.com](https://www.alphaspread.com/security/nasdaq/txn/relative-valuation/ratio/enterprise-value-to-sales))
